(deep branch of transverse cervical arte: Deep branch of transverse cervical artery (dorsal scapular artery)
Supplies the rhomboids and joins the scapular anastomosis.
(superficial branch of transverse cervic: Superficial branch of transverse cervical artery
(ulnar recurrent artery): Branch that runs back up to the anastomosis around the elbow.
abdominal aorta: Runs from T12 to its bifurcation at L4; gives the coeliac trunk and the mesenteric, renal and gonadal arteries. Its aneurysms are most often infrarenal.
accessory branch of middle meningeal art: Accessory branch of middle meningeal artery
Small branch that may enter the skull through the foramen ovale.
accessory hemi-azygos vein: Collects the upper and middle left intercostal veins.
angular artery: Terminal branch of the facial artery at the medial angle of the eye; anastomoses with the ophthalmic artery.
angular vein: Connects with the superior ophthalmic vein at the medial angle of the eye.
anterior basal segmental artery of left: Anterior basal segmental artery of left lung
Branch of the pulmonary artery to a segment of the left lung; it runs with the segmental bronchus and carries deoxygenated blood to the alveoli.
anterior basal segmental artery of right: Anterior basal segmental artery of right lung
Branch of the pulmonary artery to a segment of the right lung; it runs with the segmental bronchus and carries deoxygenated blood to the alveoli.
anterior branch of renal artery: Branch to four segments of the kidney; the segmental arteries are end arteries.
anterior cerebral artery: Supplies the medial surface of the hemisphere; its occlusion causes marked weakness and sensory loss in the opposite leg.
anterior circumflex humeral artery: Winds round the front of the surgical neck of the humerus.
anterior circumflex humeral vein: Accompanies the artery of the same name.
anterior communicating artery: Joins the two anterior cerebral arteries; the commonest site of aneurysms (can cause a bitemporal visual field defect).
anterior division of internal iliac arte: Anterior division of internal iliac artery
Gives the visceral branches (umbilical, vesical, uterine/rectal) and the obturator, internal pudendal and inferior gluteal arteries.
anterior ethmoidal artery: Supplies the anterior ethmoidal cells and the front of the nasal cavity.
anterior inferior cerebellar artery: Lower branch of the basilar artery; gives the labyrinthine artery.
anterior inferior pancreaticoduodenal ar: Branch supplying the front of the head of the pancreas.
anterior intercavernous sinus: Joins the two cavernous sinuses in front of the pituitary.
anterior interventricular artery: Descends in the anterior interventricular groove to the apex; supplies the anterior 2/3 of the septum and the anterior wall of the left ventricle. The coronary artery most often occluded ('widow maker').
anterior jugular vein: Descends in the front of the neck close to the midline.
anterior papillary muscle of right ventr: Anterior papillary muscle of right ventricle
The largest papillary muscle of the right ventricle; linked to the moderator band, it holds the tricuspid cusps through the chordae tendineae.
anterior segmental artery of left lung: Anterior segmental artery of left lung
Branch of the pulmonary artery to a segment of the left lung; it runs with the segmental bronchus and carries deoxygenated blood to the alveoli.
anterior segmental artery of right lung: Anterior segmental artery of right lung
Branch of the pulmonary artery to a segment of the right lung; it runs with the segmental bronchus and carries deoxygenated blood to the alveoli.
anterior semilunar leaflet of pulmonary: Anterior semilunar cusp of pulmonary valve
The anterior semilunar cusp of the pulmonary valve.
anterior septal branches of anterior eth: Anterior septal branches of anterior ethmoidal artery
Supply the anterosuperior part of the nasal septum.
anterior spinal artery: Formed by branches of both vertebral arteries; supplies the anterior 2/3 of the spinal cord. When it is occluded, dorsal column sensation is spared.
anterior temporal branch: Supplies the front of the temporal lobe.
anterior tibial artery: Passes over the interosseous membrane into the anterior compartment; becomes the dorsalis pedis at the ankle.
anterior tibial veins: Accompanies the artery of the same name.
anterior vein of left lung: Runs in the plane between segments and carries oxygenated blood to the pulmonary veins; it marks the segment boundaries in segmentectomy.
anterior vein of right lung: Runs in the plane between segments and carries oxygenated blood to the pulmonary veins; it marks the segment boundaries in segmentectomy.
aortic arch: Curves backwards over the left bronchus at T4; gives the brachiocephalic trunk, left common carotid and left subclavian arteries.
apical segmental artery of left lung: Apical segmental artery of left lung
Branch of the pulmonary artery to a segment of the left lung; it runs with the segmental bronchus and carries deoxygenated blood to the alveoli.
apical segmental artery of right lung: Apical segmental artery of right lung
Branch of the pulmonary artery to a segment of the right lung; it runs with the segmental bronchus and carries deoxygenated blood to the alveoli.
apical vein of right lung: Runs in the plane between segments and carries oxygenated blood to the pulmonary veins; it marks the segment boundaries in segmentectomy.
apicoposterior vein of left lung: Runs in the plane between segments and carries oxygenated blood to the pulmonary veins; it marks the segment boundaries in segmentectomy.
appendicular artery: End artery running along the edge of the mesoappendix; ligated in appendicectomy.
arcuate artery: Branch forming an arch over the bases of the metatarsals on the dorsum of the foot.
artery of central sulcus: Supplies the face and arm areas of the motor and sensory cortex.
artery of pterygoid canal: Thin branch passing through the pterygoid canal.
ascending aorta: The part that rises from the left ventricle inside the pericardium; its only branches are the coronary arteries. Type A dissection starts here.
ascending branch of left colic artery: Ascending branch of left colic artery
Anastomoses with the middle colic artery towards the splenic flexure.
ascending pharyngeal artery: Thin branch supplying the pharyngeal wall.
axillary artery: Runs from the outer border of the 1st rib to the lower border of teres major; divided into three parts by pectoralis minor.
axillary vein: Formed by the union of the basilic and brachial veins.
azygos vein: Rises on the right of the spine in the posterior mediastinum and arches at T4 into the superior vena cava; a collateral route when the IVC is blocked.
basilar artery: Artery in the groove on the front of the pons; supplies the brainstem and cerebellum and divides at its top into the posterior cerebral arteries. Its occlusion can cause locked-in syndrome.
basilic vein: Rises on the inner side of the arm; preferred for PICC lines.
bifurcation of pulmonary trunk: Where the trunk divides into right and left branches; joined to the aortic arch by the ligamentum arteriosum. A massive pulmonary embolus can form a 'saddle thrombus' here.
brachial artery: Runs in the medial bicipital groove of the arm; heard when measuring blood pressure and divides at the elbow into the radial and ulnar arteries. Can be injured in supracondylar fractures (Volkmann's contracture).
brachial veins: Paired veins accompanying the brachial artery.
brachiocephalic trunk: First branch of the aortic arch; divides behind the right sternoclavicular joint into the right common carotid and right subclavian arteries.
branch to angular gyrus: Terminal branch supplying the angular gyrus.
buccal artery: Supplies the buccinator and the mucosa of the cheek.
calcaneal branches of fibular artery: Supply the lateral part of the heel.
calcaneal branches of posterior tibial a: Calcaneal branches of posterior tibial artery
Supply the medial part of the heel.
callosomarginal artery: Branch running in the cingulate sulcus.
cavernous sinus: Sinus beside the sella turcica; the internal carotid artery and abducens nerve pass through it, and CN III, IV, V1 and V2 in its wall. Its thrombosis causes multiple cranial nerve palsies.
central retinal artery: End artery entering the optic nerve to supply the inner layers of the retina; its occlusion causes sudden painless loss of vision and a 'cherry-red spot'.
cephalic vein: Rises on the lateral side of the arm and opens through the deltopectoral groove into the axillary vein; can be used for pacemaker leads.
circumflex artery of heart: Winds round to the back of the heart in the left AV groove; supplies the left atrium and the lateral and posterior walls of the left ventricle.
circumflex scapular artery: Passes through the triangular space to join the scapular anastomosis.
circumflex scapular vein: Accompanies the artery of the same name.
coeliac trunk: Main anterior branch of the aorta at T12; divides into the left gastric, splenic and common hepatic arteries to supply the foregut (stomach, liver, spleen, part of the pancreas).
colic branch of ileocolic artery: Supplies the beginning of the ascending colon.
common facial vein: Union of the facial vein and the anterior division of the retromandibular vein.
common hepatic artery: Runs to the right and divides into the gastroduodenal and proper hepatic arteries.
common iliac artery: Arises at the aortic bifurcation at L4; divides in front of the sacroiliac joint into the internal and external iliac arteries.
common iliac vein: The left common iliac vein can be compressed under the right common iliac artery (May–Thurner syndrome).
common interosseous artery: Short trunk that divides into the anterior and posterior interosseous arteries.
common palmar digital arteries: Branches running from the superficial arch to the clefts between the fingers.
common plantar digital arteries: Branches running to the clefts between the toes.
coronary sinus: Wide venous channel in the posterior AV groove of the heart; collects the cardiac veins and opens into the right atrium.
costocervical trunk: Trunk giving the deep cervical and supreme intercostal arteries.
deep artery of penis: Runs within the corpus cavernosum and gives the helicine arteries that produce erection.
deep brachial artery: Runs with the radial nerve in the spiral groove.
deep cervical artery: Supplies the muscles of the back of the neck.
deep dorsal vein of penis: Opens into the prostatic venous plexus.
deep external pudendal artery: Deep branch supplying the skin of the perineum.
deep femoral artery: Main artery of the thigh muscles; gives the circumflex and perforating branches.
deep palmar arch: Arch formed by the radial artery at the level of the bases of the metacarpals.
deep plantar artery: Passes through the 1st metatarsal space to the sole and completes the plantar arch.
deep venous palmar arch: Accompanies the deep palmar arterial arch.
descending branch of lateral circumflex: Descending branch of lateral circumflex femoral artery
Descends along vastus lateralis; the pedicle of the anterolateral thigh flap.
descending branch of left colic artery: Descending branch of left colic artery
distal lateral striate branches: Perforating branches supplying the lateral part of the lentiform nucleus.
dorsal artery of penis: Runs on the dorsum of the penis on each side of the deep dorsal vein.
dorsal carpal anastomosis: Arterial network on the back of the wrist.
dorsal carpal branch of ulnar artery: Dorsal carpal branch of ulnar artery
Joins the network on the back of the wrist.
dorsal digital arteries of foot: Supply the dorsal surface of the toes.
dorsal digital arteries of hand: Supply the dorsal surface of the fingers.
dorsal digital veins of foot: Drain the backs of the toes.
dorsal digital veins of hand: Drain the backs of the fingers.
dorsal metacarpal arteries: Arteries between the metacarpals on the back of the hand.
dorsal metatarsal arteries: Branches from the arcuate artery to the clefts between the toes.
dorsal metatarsal veins: Open into the dorsal venous arch of the foot.
dorsal venous arch of foot: Arch from which the great and small saphenous veins begin.
dorsal venous network of hand: Superficial network often used for venous cannulation.
dorsalis pedis artery: Its pulse is felt on the dorsum of the foot lateral to the extensor hallucis longus tendon.
external carotid artery: Supplies most of the neck and face; it has eight branches (superior thyroid, lingual, facial, ascending pharyngeal, occipital, posterior auricular, maxillary, superficial temporal).
external iliac artery: Becomes the femoral artery after passing under the inguinal ligament; gives the inferior epigastric and deep circumflex iliac branches.
external iliac vein: Continuation of the femoral vein in the pelvis.
external jugular vein: Descends obliquely over sternocleidomastoid; becomes distended in right heart failure.
external pudendal veins: Open into the great saphenous vein.
facial artery: Its pulse is felt at the edge of the mandible in front of masseter; it supplies the face by a tortuous course.
facial vein: Having no valves, it lets infections of the 'danger triangle' of the face spread through the ophthalmic veins to the cavernous sinus.
femoral artery: Its pulse is felt at the middle of the inguinal ligament; it passes from the femoral triangle into the adductor canal. A common access site for cardiac catheterisation.
femoral vein: Runs medial to the artery in the femoral triangle; a common site of deep vein thrombosis.
fibular artery: Arises from the posterior tibial artery and descends along the fibula; the pedicle of the free fibula flap.
first posterior intercostal artery: Arises from the supreme intercostal artery.
frontal branch of superficial temporal a: Frontal branch of superficial temporal artery
Supplies the skin of the forehead.
frontal branches of callosomarginal arte: Supply the medial surface of the frontal lobe.
gastroduodenal artery: Descends behind the 1st part of the duodenum; a posterior duodenal ulcer can erode it and cause severe bleeding.
great cardiac vein: Vein that accompanies the LAD and opens into the coronary sinus.
great saphenous vein: The longest vein of the body; begins in front of the medial malleolus and opens into the femoral vein at the saphenous opening. Used as a coronary bypass graft; the commonest site of varicose veins.
greater palatine artery: Supplies the hard palate; passes through the incisive canal to the nose and contributes to septal bleeding.
hemi-azygos vein: Collects the lower left intercostal veins and crosses to the azygos vein at T8–T9.
hepatic portal vein: Formed behind the neck of the pancreas by the splenic and superior mesenteric veins; brings 75% of the liver's blood. Oesophageal varices develop in portal hypertension.
hepatic veins: The three large veins of the liver; they open directly into the inferior vena cava, and their occlusion is the Budd–Chiari syndrome.
ileocolic artery: Last branch, supplying the terminal ileum, caecum and appendix.
iliacus branch of iliolumbar artery: Supplies the iliacus muscle and the ilium.
iliolumbar artery: Supplies the iliacus and the muscles of the lower back.
iliolumbar vein: Accompanies the artery of the same name.
inferior alveolar artery: Supplies the lower teeth in the mandibular canal.
inferior basal vein of left lung: Inferior basal vein of left lung
Runs in the plane between segments and carries oxygenated blood to the pulmonary veins; it marks the segment boundaries in segmentectomy.
inferior basal vein of right lung: Inferior basal vein of right lung
Runs in the plane between segments and carries oxygenated blood to the pulmonary veins; it marks the segment boundaries in segmentectomy.
inferior epigastric artery: Arises from the external iliac artery and enters the rectus sheath; the landmark separating direct from indirect inguinal hernias (an indirect hernia emerges lateral to it).
inferior gluteal artery: Emerges below piriformis; supplies gluteus maximus.
inferior lateral genicular artery: Branch of the anastomosis around the knee joint.
inferior leaflet of right atrioventricul: The posteroinferior cusp of the tricuspid valve.
inferior lingular artery of left lung: Inferior lingular segmental artery of left lung
Branch of the pulmonary artery to a segment of the left lung; it runs with the segmental bronchus and carries deoxygenated blood to the alveoli.
inferior lingular vein of left lung: Inferior lingular vein of left lung
Runs in the plane between segments and carries oxygenated blood to the pulmonary veins; it marks the segment boundaries in segmentectomy.
inferior lobar artery of left lung: Inferior lobar artery of left lung
Branch of the pulmonary artery to the lower lobe of the left lung.
